title: Superlinear separation between linear and centered colorings
summary: A vertex-coloring of a graph is centered if every connected subgraph has a vertex with a unique color. A vertex-coloring of a graph is linear if every path in the graph has a vertex with a unique color. Let $χ_{\mathrm{cen}}(G)$ and $χ_{\mathrm{lin}}(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a centered (resp. linear) coloring of $G$. We present a family of graphs witnessing that if $f$ is a nondecreasing function such that $χ_{\mathrm{cen}}(G) \leq f(χ_{\mathrm{lin}}(G))$ for every graph $G$, then $f(k) = Ω(k^2 / \log k)$. The construction was found by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Pro.
